gdpr.sectionDesc: Set up your privacy notice, maps and how long data is kept.
gdpr.privacyNoticeUrlHelp: Shown in the widget so visitors can read your privacy notice before giving or refusing consent.
gdpr.privacyPolicyVersionHelp: A version label saved with every consent (e.g. v1.2, 2026-01). Change it when you update your policy and visitors will be asked for consent again.
gdpr.autoRegisterWpUsersHelp: Off by default: signed-in WordPress users chat anonymously. Turn it on and we'll register them automatically as visitors with their account name and email.
gdpr.mapTileProviderHelp: Maps come from AlphaRecall's own servers, no outside services. Choose No map to hide them: the card keeps address, hours and buttons.
gdpr.retentionHelp: Leave empty to keep them forever. You can set 1 to 3650 days. Chat messages and attachments are the exception: they are kept 90 days at most, and empty means 90.
gdpr.retentionConversationInvalid: For chat messages and attachments enter a whole number from 1 to {max}, or leave it empty. For the other data, 1 to 3650.
gdpr.retentionDisabledWarning: Automatic data cleanup isn't turned on for this server. The days you set are saved, but data won't be deleted automatically.
gdpr.retentionAttachmentsNote: Attachments: files sent in the chat stay available for this period from the upload (30 days unless you change it), and each attachment shows until when. A new value also applies to files already received: expired ones are removed within a few minutes, even when automatic data cleanup is off. If you leave it empty, files stay as long as the conversation, 90 days at most.
gdpr.retentionInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 3650, or leave it empty.

intro.title: What is waiting for you
intro.body: Only what needs your decision: chats passed to the team, appointments to confirm, new requests and the setup steps still missing. Each row has the button that does the job.

chart.title: How the week went
chart.body: Conversations, chats closed without you, contacts and visits for the last 7 or 30 days, with the day by day trend. The full report is in Statistics.

usage.title: Messages used
usage.body: How many AI messages you have used this month out of your plan. If you get close to the limit, open the plan from here.

recent.title: Recent activity
recent.body: The latest things that happened: visits booked, new contacts, requests, feedback and site syncs.

intro.title: Conversations and visitors
intro.body: Two views: Conversations lists every chat, Visitors shows the people behind them with their contact details.

list.title: Chat list
list.body: Every conversation lives here. Use search and the status filters to quickly find active or resolved chats.

detail.title: The conversation
detail.body: Read the whole exchange between the visitor and {name}. You can step in and reply yourself, rename the chat or delete it.

intro.title: What {name} brings in
intro.body: Everything {name} brings to your business is here: leads, appointments, contact requests and feedback, each in its own tab.

table.title: Check every result
table.body: Open any entry to see the details, update its status as you work on it, or delete what you don't need anymore.

export.title: Export your data
export.body: Download the list as CSV or JSON to load it into your CRM or share it with your team.

sync.title: Sync your site content
sync.body: Bring your pages and posts into {name}'s knowledge base. The more useful content it knows, the better it answers about your business.

indexed.title: What {name} knows
indexed.body: Everything {name} has learned from. You can rename entries, keep certain pages out of answers or remove them completely.

upload.title: Upload documents
upload.body: Add PDFs and other files (price lists, brochures, manuals) so {name} can answer questions about them too.

actions.title: Build your FAQs
actions.body: Add questions and answers by hand, let the AI create them from your site, or import them from a file.

categories.title: Sort them into categories
categories.body: Group your FAQs by topic. Visitors find them neatly sorted in the widget's FAQ tab, and {name} uses them to give more precise answers.

list.title: Manage your entries
list.body: Turn individual FAQs on or off, edit them and drag them to reorder. FAQs you turn off stay saved but visitors won't see them.

intro.title: What your tools collect
intro.body: The data {name}'s tools collect: appointments, email leads, chats handed off to a human and product searches, each in its own tab.

table.title: Keep things tidy
table.body: Check every entry and delete the ones you've already handled. The same data also shows up in the Activity Log.

widget.title: Customization
widget.body: Choose how the chat looks on your site: colors, position, theme, chat button style and welcome message, with a live preview.

agent.title: Training
agent.body: The content, business details and FAQs your assistant learns from, plus how it talks (name, tone, role) and which tools it can use, like booking appointments or collecting leads.

team.title: Team and access
team.body: Add the people who reply in chats, and choose who can get into this dashboard and with which role.

privacy.title: Privacy and data
privacy.body: Privacy notice and consent, visitor identification, maps and how long data is kept, all in one place.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body: Choose which emails you get (appointments, requests, feedback) and where {name} should alert your team when a human is needed.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.body: Options for going deeper: custom widget CSS, plus shortcuts to run setup again or replay these tours.

legacyAccess.title: Earlier access rules
legacyAccess.description: These rules come from the old team list and still apply, even over WordPress roles. Remove them and access will depend only on the Support team and the site administrators.
legacyAccess.removeBody: From now on their access depends only on their WordPress role: Support team or site administrator. With neither, they cannot open the dashboard.
legacyAccess.removeFailed: We could not remove the rule. Try again.
legacyAccess.lastOwner: This is the only active owner rule: it cannot be removed.
